scope: Recorded field feedback; suggested changes are not approved specifications.

record.event: P001@r1 and follow-on D000@r21 ran together in one L2 gate (trace 20261124T143253Z-5cd962, started with `canon.py trace start gate P001 D000 --tier L2`), following workflow.md:103 (`canon.py approvals GATE --start ID@rN ...` with the full first round). Running `canon.py approvals P001-r1 --start P001@r1 D000@r21` failed with `canon: D000@r21 does not belong to gate P001-r1`, forcing inspection of canon.py:2826,2841 to learn that approvals forbids mixing P and D IDs under one gate key and requires separate D000-r21 and P001-r1 records.
record.suggestion: Either allow `canon.py approvals` to record a plan gate together with its follow-on design target(s) under one gate key (matching `trace start gate P001 D000`), or state explicitly in workflow.md Gate status and `approvals -h` that plan and design L2 approvals must be recorded under separate P*-r* and D*-r* gate keys.

record.event: Both P001-r1/baseline.txt and D002-r9/baseline.txt recorded the 7-character short hash `fff71d4` instead of a 40-character full commit OID. `canon.py trace end` succeeded with exit 0 and zero warning while `retain_review_input()` (canon.py:4968) returned early, leaving `review_input=unknown` in `trace history` for both 20261124T143253Z-5cd962 and 20261124T154711Z-52babc.
record.suggestion: Have `retain_review_input()` resolve unambiguous abbreviated commit hashes via `git rev-parse --verify <baseline>^{commit}` (or warn on stderr / reject non-40-hex baseline.txt at trace end) instead of silently dropping `review_input` to `unknown`.

record.step: Launch: asynchronous host subagent alongside command reviewer
record.event: Following Launch ('Start each command reviewer once on a retained host job ... then launch the host reviewers asynchronously'), P001-r1 Confirm 3 ran blocking Shell(block_until_ms: 1800000) alongside background Task(run_in_background: true) in Cursor (transcript L116). After Shell returned at 00:18, the agent yielded waiting for the background Task notification, which never fired; the chat stalled silently for 16 minutes until the user asked at 00:34 (L119), when subagents/535c3a5c-6b28-4920-be72-b20a094021ba.jsonl already held the completed report (L120). Confirm 4–6 ran blocking Shell and foreground Task(run_in_background: false) in one parallel batch with zero missed notifications.
record.suggestion: Note under Launch that on hosts supporting parallel blocking tool calls (such as Cursor), running the command reviewer and host subagent reviewer(s) together in one parallel foreground tool batch avoids dropped async completion notices; and when any background subagent remains open at turn end, check its host transcript file before yielding to the user.

record.step: Confirmation: new blockers repeating across confirmation rounds
record.event: During P001-r1, fixes to cross-family:F6 (fork probe cache) produced 6 cross-family confirmation rounds (cross-family-confirm.md through cross-family-confirm-6.md) and 5 same-model confirmation rounds (D002-r9/same-model-confirm.md through same-model-confirm-5.md) resolving 7 confirmation-introduced blockers (B1–B7, ~50 minutes wall time before escalating to the user at Confirm 4). Confirmation says 'Blockers still open after this round go to the user' for unresolved findings, but gives no escalation trigger when fixes introduce new blockers across confirmation rounds, nor does `trace end`/`trace recheck` distinguish first-confirmation new blockers from later confirmation rounds.
record.suggestion: Clarify in Confirmation that if a confirmation round still ends with any open blocker—including a new blocker introduced by a fix—stop and escalate to the user (or route through a focused design/prototype pass) rather than looping unbounded fix-confirm passes; and clarify how multi-round confirmation-introduced blockers should be counted in `new_blockers` and archived.

record.step: Records and Pick: linked worktree .canon/canon-retro/ path
record.event: Running /canon-retro in linked worktree .worktrees/plan-d003-ring-protocol found no .canon/canon-retro/ directory there, while the main checkout /home/lihaol/silk/.canon/canon-retro/ held 26 causes (notes.md) and 30 skill-friction entries (skills.jsonl). canon/SKILL.md routes trace data to the main checkout's trace directory while declaring a worktree's .canon/ its own, and canon-retro/SKILL.md names only relative .canon/canon-retro/ with no linked-worktree rule, risking split history and lost retro notes when the worktree is removed.
record.suggestion: State in canon-retro/SKILL.md (and canon/SKILL.md Concurrent work) that notes.md and skills.jsonl live under the main checkout's .canon/canon-retro/ (via git rev-parse --git-common-dir), matching trace storage, so linked worktrees read and update one repository retro ledger.

record.step: trace end --dir: mtime archive filter on restarted gate in same topic directory
record.event: After cancelling L1 gate 20261125T030511Z-c78316 (started 11:05:11) and restarting P002@r1 as L2 gate 20261125T030845Z-82bb16 (started 11:08:45) in .canon/canon-blind-review/P002-r1/, trace end --dir archived only files modified since 11:08:45 and silently omitted pre-existing baseline.txt (11:05:11) and same-model-prompt.md (11:05:23), leaving trace history reporting archive=ok (files present) with review_input=unknown and an incomplete prompt archive.
record.suggestion: Have trace end --dir always include baseline.txt, snapshot.txt, and prompt/report files for every recorded reviewer key regardless of mtime (or warn when baseline.txt/prompt files exist in --dir with older mtimes), and note in canon-blind-review to clear or touch the topic directory when restarting a cancelled gate.

record.step: Tiers: L1 vs L2 for a first implementation plan under an existing unimplemented L2 design
record.event: Following Tiers ('L1: multi-step work under an existing design that needs a plan'; 'L2: a new topic with no owning design, a new module...'), the agent started P002@r1 (the first implementation plan for accepted-but-unimplemented L2 design D003, inside existing scaffold dir src/ring/) as L1 (20261125T030045Z-e9d7f9, 20261125T030511Z-c78316). The user interrupted to question the tier and upgraded P002@r1 to L2 (20261125T030845Z-82bb16), where cross-family Astra caught 3 unique blockers and 9 unique majors same-model missed.
record.suggestion: Clarify in canon/SKILL.md Tiers (and canon-plan/SKILL.md) whether the first implementation plan for an L2 design without an implemented revision inherits L2 (or defaults to L2 when unsure) even when an L0 scaffold already created the module directory.

record.step: trace recheck: confirmation-introduced blockers have no finding key
record.event: In both D003@r32 (20261125T020012Z-aaf2cd: 3+1 confirmation-introduced blockers across recheck and recheck-2) and P002@r1 (20261125T030845Z-82bb16: same-model:F12 and cross-family:F17–F21 across recheck, recheck2, recheck3), canon.py trace recheck only accepts first-round merged finding keys (e.g. cross-family:F10, cross-family:F16) and has no syntax to record targeted rechecks of confirmation-introduced blockers, leaving those recheck passes unlinked in trace history.
record.suggestion: Allow trace recheck (or trace end --input) to record confirmation-introduced blockers and their subsequent targeted recheck results (e.g. a confirm-finding key or --new-blocker ref) so multi-pass confirmation telemetry is complete.

record.event: Running canon.py show with 8 section slugs (D003#caller-streams D003#publishing ... D003#verification) exited 2 with unrecognized arguments because show accepts only one ID#slug per call (unlike which, affected and check), forcing multiple shell round-trips or falling back to raw Read with offsets on a 192 KB design doc.
record.suggestion: Accept multiple ID or ID#slug arguments in one canon.py show invocation, separated by a header per target.
